description:
Approved implementation plan, 2026-11-28: agents select authorized documents from disk or Google Drive and users receive attachments in Mattermost, email, BO chat and web widget. User approved the six-step scope/sequence in this conversation. This revision prepares the existing epic for implementation; no feature implementation has started in this turn.

## Stack and boundaries
PR6 worktree ../zaq-feat-attach-documents, branch feat/attach-documents, current parent 6a546dc44a581013608b3d8a8f4efa138d357c38 verified on 2026-11-28. Reference ../zaq-feat-channel-files supplies examples, not architecture authority. No Git mutations or external publication authorized here. PR4 owns separate Channel-local planning; PR5 owns preparation, execution, outcomes and confirmation. PR6 reuses and extends web transport integration where needed. PR7 owns RunAgent, NotifyPerson and notification/workflow integration.

## Reuse and execution contract
New Action AttachDocuments reuses GetDocument through validated ActionContract/Jido.Exec, Record authorization/provenance and TrustedContext. Extend existing schema-based opaque aliases and StreamEvents completion collection; preserve its invocation correlation/replay handling. Executor and canonical Outgoing builder carry records in Outgoing.attachments, never Outgoing.Delivery. Channels reuse PR4/PR5 planning/execution. Selection does not download, upload or filter for destination limits. No parallel collector, planner, ACL implementation or provider downloader.

## Core selection acceptance
1. Use Outgoing.attachments only; never port Outgoing.Delivery, delivery.error, Agent plans or prepared payloads. No selection-stage transport validation, file-size filtering, file acquisition or failure-notice send path. Include all valid selected Records; PR5 applies selected-connection settings and transport policy later.
2. Trusted context.actor is the caller identity. ActorNormalizer and literal top-level skip_permissions == true are authoritative; no flat person_id/team_ids, model-supplied actor or nil-identity elevation. Enforce file kind and authentic provenance even for explicitly privileged callers. Data-source selections refresh current authorized metadata with signed provider/config/file claims; generic signed Records require current Record authorization.
3. Add/remove/replace apply atomically per authorized instruction in native declaration order. Authorization failure rejects that instruction and leaves prior selection intact; successful earlier/later calls survive partial failure across calls. add deduplicates stable source identity; remove only deselects; replace [] clears exactly. Same ID on different provider/config scopes never collapses. Failed/malformed calls stay tool feedback/private safe evidence, do not clear valid selection or poison transport. A successful retry has ordinary successful selection semantics.
4. Only a current pending native request can select. Match trusted tool/invocation identity and ignore replay, foreign-request, late and post-terminal events. Alias lifetime stays logical-server-scoped; selection lifetime stays request-scoped. Failure, cancellation, worker exit, suppressed/partial error, handoff and next-request paths cannot publish or leak selected files. Existing text/trace/steering behavior remains intact.
5. Successful configured Agent results carry only the final verified Record list through StreamEvents -> Executor -> canonical Outgoing builder -> Agent role result. Empty/no-tool runs are ordinary text; incoming files never echo automatically. Model output/public status/history diagnostics must not expose full handles, provenance capabilities, raw content or runtime context.
6. A late PR5-dependent backend integration proves the final B selection (after add A/add B/remove A) is the only file materialized/sent through the existing route and confirmations reflect actual provider outcomes. Preserve PR5 failure policies, timeout/uncertainty distinctions and no automatic retries; tool success never claims delivery.


## Expanded delivery and file API acceptance
Mattermost already exists in mix.exs; verify and pin working adapter support through the existing zaq-h2i.4.3 prerequisite. Verify email MIME delivery. BO and widget require capabilities/execution, safe published attachment descriptors, presentation/download and authorized history restoration. Widget package code and release/pinning dependencies are explicit; no ignored deps edits or unshipped capability claims.
The widget file API uses the existing widget authentication/session lifecycle and ZAQ actor resolution, preserves process ownership and connector/page/runtime/expiry/revocation bindings, and authorizes the requested message attachment and current source access before bytes are fetched. Reuse data-source operations and materialization via NodeRouter. A signed materialization handle is a bearer locator, not sufficient browser authorization. URLs never expose it or grant independent access. BO retains its separate BO session boundary and shares authorized source retrieval.
Acceptance is disk and Google Drive x all four destinations. Check exact selected files/content, names/types, limits, partial failure and confirmation. Browser targets additionally test expiry/revocation, wrong user/widget/config, history reload, unavailable files and no source credentials/paths/handles exposure. Real configured-provider smoke evidence is distinct from external-edge fixtures; missing access remains an acceptance prerequisite, not a passed test.

The sequence intentionally serializes implementation ownership. Only .1 is an internal root. External adapter compatibility blocks its consumer; PR5 route is already closed. Parent epic closure never blocks child acceptance. Human UX approval follows implementation/acceptance; only then author the consolidated browser journeys, followed by technical review, coverage and final validation.

## Handoff and authorization
Implementation handoff: Scope and sequence approved by the user on 2026-11-28. This turn records the plan only; application implementation, commits, pushes, rebases and dependency publication are not performed or authorized by this planning update. Read AGENTS.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/documentation.md, docs/conventions.md and docs/code-quality.md before execution. Read applicable service guides and module responsibilities; Agent work requires the harness-critical checks; BO work requires DESIGN.md and docs/bo-components.md. Recheck live source and dependency contracts. Preserve existing test behavior unless specifically approved. Write immediate unit/integration/property tests before corresponding code; new browser journeys wait for the human UX gate. Keep real internal boundaries, mock only external edges, and inject runtime dependencies through existing opts/context and Zaq.Config. Follow the owning validation lifecycle. PR7 owns RunAgent, NotifyPerson and notification/workflow integration.

Environment readiness is not established by this plan. Recheck isolated database, dependencies, tools and historical setup blocker in .1. Apply owner documentation updates with implementation; no separate execution-plan document or duplicate epic. Planning update validation checks issue descriptions, graph acyclicity, reciprocal dependency links and intended roots; application tests are not applicable to tracker-only changes.
